headline: Jake O'Brien to leave Everton?
standfirst: The 25-year-old is keen to play more games in his preferred position of centre-back.
body:
Everton are expected to listen to offers for Jake O’Brien, with the defender attracting interest from clubs in England and Europe ahead of next week’s transfer deadline.

The Republic of Ireland international, 25, spent much of last season as a makeshift right-back but is keen to be a regular starter in his preferred central defensive role, something Everton are unable to guarantee at this stage, and would be open to a move that provides this. The expectation from sources briefed on the situation, speaking anonymously to protect relationships, is that the Merseyside club will now be open to offers for his services.

O’Brien was an unused substitute in Saturday’s 2-0 victory over former side Crystal Palace, with captain James Tarkowski and Jarrad Branthwaite starting as the central pairing and the versatile Merlin Rohl filling in on the right.

He is the subject of interest from clubs in England, Italy and France ahead of next Tuesday’s deadline. A departure would leave Everton with just three senior options, the other being Michael Keane, and almost certainly needing to strengthen in central defence. They remain on the lookout for a new right-back and have shown interest in Palace’s Daniel Munoz and Fulham’s Timothy Castagne, among others.

Everton are also anticipating offers for striker Beto, who is on the radar of clubs in Italy. Chelsea’s Liam Delap is one player admired by manager David Moyes and his coaching staff, should the Guinea-Bissau international depart.

O’Brien joined Everton in a £17million ($23.2m) deal from French side Lyon in 2024. He made 37 Premier League appearances last season, with just five coming in the centre of defence.

Everton travel to Championship side Preston North End on Wednesday for a Carabao Cup second-round tie, before facing Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium on Saturday.

O’Brien exit would leave Everton short
Analysis from Everton correspondent Patrick Boyland

It was not so long ago that O’Brien was widely considered the future of the Everton defence alongside England international Branthwaite.

Standing at 6ft 6in (198cm) and quick across the ground, O’Brien has impressed in his fleeting appearances at centre-back. He performed admirably last season in a makeshift right-sided role, but was still quite evidently a square peg in a round hole. While Moyes liked his extra height and defensive nous, his lack of attacking game often left the side’s wingers isolated.
author: Owner

headline: Dara Fitzgerald's senior debut, straight off the bench
standfirst: The 18-year-old came on at Turner's Cross to a standing ovation in his first pro appearance.
body:
Turner's Cross has seen plenty of debuts. Not many get eighteen minutes and a standing ovation.

Dara Fitzgerald came on with the game gone, but the reception told you what the ground thinks of him. He has come through every underage level from U15 up.

Cork City have been careful with him. On this evidence they won't be able to be for much longer.
author: Footballers Staff

headline: Josh Cullen reaches 250 club appearances
standfirst: Marked with a clean sheet and the armband at Turf Moor.
body:
Two hundred and fifty games is a career in itself.

Cullen got there in the least dramatic way possible — ninety minutes at the base of midfield, 94% of his passes finding a teammate, and a clean sheet at the end of it.

He wore the armband for the occasion.
author: Footballers Staff
